mascot: Fraction Farah — a friendly baker with a round chapati, a rolling pin and a famous fair-share smile

slides.title: One Whole Roti 🫓
slides.text: This is ONE WHOLE roti — nothing broken, nothing missing! When we cut a whole into equal pieces, each piece gets a special name. Fractions begin here!
slides.spoken: One whole means nothing is cut away yet.

slides.title: The HALF (1/2) 🍕
slides.text: Cut the roti into 2 EQUAL parts — each part is called a HALF! Two halves put together make 1 whole. We write half as 1/2.
slides.spoken: Two equal parts: each one is a half.

slides.title: Equal Parts Matter! ⚖️
slides.text: Careful! A half must be an EQUAL part. If you cut one big bit and one small bit, neither is a true half! Both parts must be exactly the same size.
slides.spoken: Only equal parts can be called halves.

slides.title: The QUARTER (1/4) 🍰
slides.text: Cut the roti into 4 EQUAL parts — each part is a QUARTER! Four quarters make 1 whole. We write quarter as 1/4.
slides.spoken: Four equal parts: each one is a quarter.

slides.title: 2 Quarters = 1 Half! 💡
slides.text: Here is a secret: two quarters make one half! Take 2 of the 4 equal parts — that is exactly half the roti. Half of 4 pieces is 2 pieces!
slides.spoken: Two quarters joined together equal one half.

challenges.question: Amma cuts a roti into 2 EQUAL parts. What is each part called?
challenges.hint: Two equal parts — each one has a special name!
challenges.misconception: Two equal parts mean each part is a half.

challenges.question: How many halves make 1 whole?
challenges.hint: Put two half-rotis together — what do you get?
challenges.misconception: Two halves join to make one whole.

challenges.question: A chapati is cut into 4 EQUAL parts. One part is called?
challenges.misconception: One part out of 4 equal parts is a quarter.

challenges.question: How many quarters make 1 whole?
challenges.hint: All 4 equal pieces together make the whole roti!
challenges.misconception: Four quarters join to make one whole.

challenges.question: Which roti shows EQUAL parts?
options: One big part and one small part
challenges.hint: Fractions need parts that are exactly the same size!
challenges.misconception: Only equal parts can be called halves or quarters.

challenges.question: Sort each sharing by how much of the SAME roti it is!
challenges.hint: Half means 1 of 2 equal shares. Quarter means 1 of 4 equal shares.
challenges.misconception: 4 of 8 and 5 of 10 are halves. 2 of 8 and 3 of 12 are quarters.

challenges.question: Diya cuts an apple into 2 equal parts and eats 1 part. How much apple is LEFT?
challenges.hint: The apple had 2 equal parts. One part is gone. One is left!
challenges.misconception: One of the two halves remains, so half the apple is left.

challenges.question: Which is MORE: half of the SAME laddoo, or a quarter of it?
challenges.hint: More pieces means smaller pieces: 2 parts or 4 parts?
challenges.misconception: A half is 1 of 2 big equal parts; a quarter is 1 of 4 smaller parts. Half is more.
